intro: Japanese has three verbs for 'give', and the choice depends on the direction of the gift and whose point of view you tell it from. Picture an arrow from giver to receiver, with you and your side (family, your team, whoever you speak for) at the centre. あげる: the arrow points away from you, or passes between other people. くれる: the arrow points at you or your side. もらう: the same event told by the receiver, 'I got it from ...'. First ask where the arrow points, then pick the verb.

skills.rule: Use あげる when the thing moves away from me or my side, or between two other people; it never points towards me.
skills.explain:
あげる is 'give' seen from the giver's side. The frame is giver は/が, receiver に, thing を: 私は友達に本をあげた. The giver is often left out when it is me: 妹にお菓子をあげました. Between two people outside my side it is also あげる: 田中さんは山田さんに花をあげた.

The hard limit is direction. When the receiver is me or someone on my side (my family, my team) and the giver is from outside, あげる is wrong: use くれる. 'My teacher gave my brother a dictionary' is 先生が弟に辞書をくれた, because my brother is on my side.

あげる is for equals and people below you. Giving to a superior is 差し上げる. やる is the blunt plain version, used for animals and plants (犬にえさをやる), though many speakers now say あげる there too. Saying これをあげます to a superior's face sounds presumptuous; say どうぞ or 差し上げます.
patterns: [giver] は/が [receiver] に [thing] を あげる

examples.jp: 妹[いもうと]にお菓子[かし]を{あげました}。
examples.en: I gave my younger sister some sweets.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]の誕生日[たんじょうび]に花[はな]を{あげます}。
examples.en: I'm going to give my friend flowers for their birthday.

examples.jp: この本[ほん]、もう読[よ]んだから{あげる}よ。
examples.en: I've already read this book, so you can have it.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は彼氏[かれし]にマフラーを{あげた}そうです。
examples.en: I hear my older sister gave her boyfriend a scarf.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは山田[やまだ]さんにチョコレートを{あげました}。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka gave Ms Yamada some chocolates.

contrast.note: If the thing comes to me or my side from outside, the verb flips: 友達が本をくれた 'a friend gave me a book'. あげる cannot point at me.
Both use に, in opposite directions: 友達に本をあげた 'I gave my friend a book', 友達に本をもらった 'I got a book from my friend'. Read the verb, not the particle.
The humble version for a superior receiver: 先生に差し上げた. Same direction, higher respect.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]が私[わたし]に本[ほん]を{あげました}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]が本[ほん]を{くれました}。
mistakes.note: The book comes to me, so the verb must be くれる; 私に is then usually dropped.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]が弟[おとうと]に辞書[じしょ]を{あげました}。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]が弟[おとうと]に辞書[じしょ]を{くれました}。
mistakes.note: My brother is on my side, so a gift to him from an outsider is くれる.

skills.tip: Arrow leaving me, or passing between others: あげる. If it lands on me or mine, it cannot be あげる.

skills.rule: Use くれる when someone else gives to me or to someone on my side; the giver is the subject (が or は) and I am never the giver.
skills.explain:
くれる is 'give' with the arrow pointing at me. The giver is the subject (が, or は as topic), and since the receiver is obviously me, 私に is normally left out: 兄が時計をくれた 'my brother gave me a watch'. It also covers my side: 隣の人が娘にみかんをくれた 'the neighbour gave my daughter a mandarin'.

Two rules decide it. The receiver must be me or my side; a gift between two outsiders is あげる. And I can never be the giver of くれる: 'I'll give you this' is あげる, never くれる.

In a question the listener stands in the centre: 誰がくれたの？ 'Who gave it to you?' For a superior giver use the respectful くださる: 先生がくださった. Casual くれる? also asks for something: それ、くれる？ 'Can I have that?'
patterns: [giver] が/は [thing] を くれる  (to me)
[giver] が [my family member] に [thing] を くれる

examples.jp: 兄[あに]が時計[とけい]を{くれました}。
examples.en: My older brother gave me a watch.

examples.jp: 祖母[そぼ]がお小遣[こづか]いを{くれた}。
examples.en: My grandmother gave me some pocket money.

examples.jp: このペン、誰[だれ]が{くれた}の？
友達[ともだち]が旅行[りょこう]のお土産[みやげ]を{くれました}。
examples.en: A friend gave me a souvenir from their trip.

examples.jp: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]が娘[むすめ]にみかんを{くれました}。
examples.en: The neighbour gave my daughter a mandarin.

contrast.note: あげる is the outward arrow. If I am the giver, or neither person is on my side, use あげる.
Same event, other subject: 友達がくれた (friend が) = 友達にもらった (friend に). Giver with が goes with くれる; giver with に or から goes with もらう.
The respectful くれる for a superior giver: 先生がくださった. Same direction.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は弟[おとうと]にゲームを{くれました}。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は弟[おとうと]にゲームを{あげました}。
mistakes.note: I am the giver, so the arrow points away from me: あげる.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]に本[ほん]を{くれました}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]が本[ほん]を{くれました}。
mistakes.note: Meaning 'a friend gave me a book': the giver of くれる takes が. With に, say 友達に本をもらいました.

skills.tip: くれる = 'gave ME (or mine)'. If you can add 'me' or 'my ...' after 'gave', it is くれる.

skills.rule: Use もらう when the receiver is the subject: [receiver] は [giver] に or から [thing] を もらう.
skills.explain:
もらう is 'get, receive'. The subject is the receiver, usually me and often unstated, and the giver takes に or から: 父に自転車をもらった = 父から自転車をもらった 'I got a bike from my dad'. When the giver is an organisation (a company, school, city office) use から: 会社からボーナスをもらった.

The receiver is normally me or my side, though outsiders work too: 田中さんは山田さんに花をもらった. What does not work is an outsider receiving from me: 'my friend got it from me' is said 私が友達にあげた, not 友達は私にもらった.

The same event can be told two ways: 母がセーターをくれた and 母にセーターをもらった both mean my mother gave me a jumper. Choose by the particle on the giver: が goes with くれる, に or から with もらう. Receiving from a superior is the humble いただく: 先生にいただいた.
patterns: [receiver] は/が [giver] に/から [thing] を もらう
[organisation] から [thing] を もらう

examples.jp: 父[ちち]に自転車[じてんしゃ]を{もらいました}。
examples.en: I got a bicycle from my father.

examples.jp: 誕生日[たんじょうび]に何[なに]を{もらった}の？
examples.en: What did you get for your birthday?

examples.jp: 会社[かいしゃ]からボーナスを{もらいました}。
examples.en: I got a bonus from the company.

examples.jp: 妹[いもうと]は友達[ともだち]から手紙[てがみ]を{もらった}。
examples.en: My younger sister got a letter from a friend.

examples.jp: 店[みせ]の人[ひと]に地図[ちず]を{もらいました}。
examples.en: I got a map from the shop assistant.

contrast.note: Same event from the giver's side: 友達がくれた. If the giver has が, the verb is くれる; if it has に or から, もらう.
友達に本をあげた 'I gave', 友達に本をもらった 'I got'. The に is the same; only the verb tells you the direction.
The humble もらう for a superior giver: 先生にいただいた. Same particles.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]が傘[かさ]を{もらいました}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]に傘[かさ]を{もらいました}。
mistakes.note: Meaning 'I got an umbrella from a friend': with が, the friend becomes the one who got it.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]は私[わたし]に本[ほん]を{もらいました}。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は友達[ともだち]に本[ほん]を{あげました}。
mistakes.note: When I am the giver, tell it from my side with あげる.

skills.tip: If 'got it from ___' fits, the verb is もらう and ___ takes に (から for organisations).
